clue.text: Touring west of England, composer makes Land's End

indicators.note: a composer touring a place goes all around it, so his name wraps the letter

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: in an across entry west is the left-hand end, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the westernmost (first) letter of England

explanation.surface: A composer touring the West Country ends up at Land's End in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End looks like the Cornish headland, but it is the definition read literally: where the land stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is the strip of shore where dry ground finishes and the sea begins, literally the end of the land.

clue.text: Promotional material from Republican — weep digesting it

indicators.note: to digest something is to take it inside, so the weeping word swallows the party letter

parts.note: to blub is to cry, an informal British word
standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political ad campaign prompts a Republican to shed tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to Republican, the letter the weeping word takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short puffing description printed on a book jacket or advertising leaflet to sell the product.

clue.text: French creative's endless range, wretched dirge included

indicators.note: the mangled song is included within the shortened range, sitting inside it
without its end, the mountain range loses its final letter

parts.note: the Andes, the South American mountain range

indicators.note: a wretched song is in a sorry state, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French artist's limited repertoire includes a miserable funeral song.
explanation.walkthrough: Andes loses its S to leave ANDE, which then wraps the reshuffled dirge.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate, so a writer, a creative figure from France.

clue.text: Where Tony's sheltered until now

indicators.note: something sheltered is tucked away inside, so the letters sit concealed within the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks where Tony has been hiding all this time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is a formal word meaning up to this point, so it stands in for 'until now' as in 'hitherto'.

clue.text: What doctor knows about development of endemic across India?

indicators.note: the reworked letters lie across the single letter, spanning it on both sides
a development is a change of form, so the letters of the disease word are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about what a physician understands of a disease spreading throughout India.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is the science and practice of treating illness, the body of knowledge a physician has studied and practises.

clue.text: Good arrangement kid cultivated growing profitably?

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over and turned, so these letters are dug into a new order

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child has been brought up well in a sensible setting, thriving nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'cultivated' does that job and also suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Market gardening means raising vegetables and fruit commercially for sale, so cultivating crops to make money; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Untidy plate of food left out — rank!

parts.note: a dish is a plate of prepared food

indicators.note: with the abbreviation for left omitted, the rank word drops that letter

parts.note: a level is a grade or rank
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A messy plate of food has been left out and now smells foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a word for the smell, but it is a grade or level.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to make hair or clothing messy, a verb matching 'untidy' used as a verb.

clue.text: Delivered Middle Eastern folk's items from dairy

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: the Kurds are a people of the Middle East

explanation.surface: Produce from a dairy delivered to a Middle Eastern community.
explanation.definitionFit: Curds are the solid lumps formed when milk coagulates, a dairy product used to make cheese.

clue.text: Fluid penetrates recently acquired belt, breaking item

parts.note: something recently acquired is new

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so the fluid abbreviation enters the belt word

parts.note: a sash is a band worn round the waist
fl is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz

explanation.surface: Liquid seeps into a brand-new belt and it breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' seems to be what the belt does, but it is part of the definition: breaking news.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief urgent bulletin interrupting broadcasts, an item of breaking news.

clue.text: Violent criminal crows about making a comeback

parts.note: a murder is the collective noun for a group of crows

indicators.note: a word making a comeback returns the way it came, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A thug squawks about returning to the scene of the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crows' reads as a verb for boasting, but it is the birds, whose collective noun is a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer is a person who unlawfully kills another, as violent a criminal as there is.

clue.text: Back from class wanting swim, dash off

indicators.note: the lone letter is in want of a swim, so the stroke follows it
the back of the word is its tail end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of class
the crawl is a swimming stroke, front crawl

explanation.surface: Back from school and longing for a swim, a pupil hurries off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash off' sounds like leaving in a hurry, but here it means writing something quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to write hastily and messily, just as dashing off a note means writing it quickly.

clue.text: Thingamabob's in goal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thing whose name escapes you
second meaning: an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Some unnamed whatsit has ended up in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in goal' suggests a football net or goalkeeper; goal is simply an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is a physical thing of any kind, and also the purpose of an action, as in the object of the exercise.

clue.text: Observe person voting in debate

indicators.note: a debate is conducted in speech, so the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: in Parliament those voting yes are the ayes

explanation.surface: Watch a member casting their vote during a parliamentary debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so it matches watching or observing as a verb.

clue.text: Clarinet's often somewhat quiet

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of letters is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A remark that the clarinet tends to sound rather subdued.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and quiet both describe a low volume of sound, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Unwanted yogurt oddly flushed away

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions are flushed away, leaving only the even ones behind

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of yogurt

explanation.surface: Some unwanted yogurt has been strangely poured down the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean rejected or no longer in favour, as in 'flares are out', so no longer wanted.

clue.text: Slowcoach in middle of Tesco initially no trouble

indicators.note: only the central letter of the supermarket name is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of Tesco, a British supermarket chain

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of no
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sluggish shopper in the middle of a supermarket is causing no bother at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail moves famously slowly, so the word is used of any dawdler or slow person.

clue.text: Reside by the banks of Uncompahgre, bighorn roaming

indicators.note: an animal roaming wanders freely, so the letters wander out of their order
a river's banks are its two edges, so only the outer letters of its name are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Uncompahgre, a river in Colorado
taken as written; a bighorn is a wild mountain sheep

explanation.surface: A bighorn sheep wanders along a Colorado riverbank where it lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour a place is to live next to or border it, so the verb means dwelling beside.

clue.text: Argentine lying about wild party filling one-third of summer

indicators.note: lying about suggests lying turned around, so the whole combination is read in the opposite direction
the party fills the gap inside the month abbreviation, going within it

parts.note: August is one of the three summer months, abbreviated AUG
a rave is a wild dance party

explanation.surface: An Argentinian lounges around a wild party in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The party goes after the A of AUG, and that whole string is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, was born in Argentina, so the surname identifies a famous Argentine.

clue.text: A group covering 'Parasites' — a favourite of Claire's?

indicators.note: a group covering a song plays its own version, so the band takes its name after the song title

parts.note: taken as written
lice are parasitic insects
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A band does a cover of a song called 'Parasites', a hit with a fan named Claire.
explanation.walkthrough: Claire's is a British high-street chain of accessory shops. 'covering' is the music sense, a band playing another's song, not putting one thing round another.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alice band is a wide hair band of the kind sold by Claire's accessory shops, so plausibly a bestseller there.

clue.text: Refurbished crib cool green

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up and rebuilt, so these letters are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A renovated baby's cot looks stylishly green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' reads as a colour or eco label, but it is a noun: a green vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens are leafy vegetables, and broccoli is a typical example of such a vegetable.

clue.text: At home, mischievous child scratches Tesla "accidentally"

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: to scratch something is to cancel or strike it out, so the unit letter is removed

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A naughty kid at home keys the family's Tesla car and claims it was an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car brand, but it is the physics unit whose symbol is T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in error means doing it by mistake, without meaning to, which is what accidentally means.

clue.text: Cardinal and Father exiting carriage

indicators.note: a priest exiting leaves the word, so his abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: freight is goods carried, or the carriage of goods
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A cardinal and a priest step out of a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal looks like the churchman, but it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers such as one, two and three, and eight is one of them.

clue.text: Returning with vital information?

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone heading back home armed with life-or-death intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' here means of life: the question mark flags that the information is genetic.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA carries the genetic code for every living thing, so it is literally information essential to life.

clue.text: Provide very strong soldiers before the day's over

indicators.note: over here means spread round, so the two letters for the day enclose the rest

parts.note: the day as in 'twice the day', meaning per day, which is A (a) plus D (day)

indicators.note: before means coming first, so the loudness marking leads and the soldiers follow

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
OR means other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Supply powerful troops before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the day' works like 'a day' in 'twice the day', so it gives A and D, which are split to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to give or supply it, as in 'the view affords a glimpse of the sea'.

clue.text: Crack injection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attempt, as in 'have a go'
second meaning: a jab from a needle

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words suggest drugs, but crack is an attempt and injection a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is both an attempt at something, like having a crack at it, and an informal word for a hypodermic jab.

clue.text: Unknown figure made pawn in poisonous matter

indicators.note: one thing made into another is swapped for it, so a letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: toxic means poisonous
x is the classic unknown quantity in algebra
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A mysterious person is used as a pawn in a toxic affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' is the definition in the sense of a subject; 'poisonous matter' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject under discussion, the matter in hand, as in 'a matter for debate'.

clue.text: Sorry leaders of underperforming club expect stick

indicators.note: something in a sorry state is a mess, so the chosen letters are jumbled
the leaders are the front runners, so only the first letter of each following word

parts.note: the initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: The bosses of a failing football club are braced for criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expect stick' reads as 'expect criticism'; stick here is the long rod used in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the tapered stick used to strike the ball in billiards, snooker and pool.

clue.text: In a hurry, leave church do

parts.note: to flee is to leave in haste
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out of a church function in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church do' looks like a parish social; 'do' is a verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece and to do someone both mean to swindle or overcharge them, an informal British sense of do.

clue.text: Drop of vino — cracking remedy for wind

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so the letter goes inside the remedy

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

indicators.note: just a drop means a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the wine is taken

parts.note: the first letter of vino

explanation.surface: A splash of wine is suggested as a great cure for flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like a digestive complaint, but it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind, as a road or river does, is to bend and turn, which is what curving means as a verb.

clue.text: Pro's opening two rounds once again rubbish

indicators.note: the opening of the word is its first letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the first letter of pro
two round letters, O and O
the three letters built so far, written out a second time

explanation.surface: A professional's opening two rounds of golf are poor again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' is a verb here, to dismiss scornfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to dismiss it contemptuously, which is what rubbishing it means.

clue.text: Great admiration for icon dancing adroitly

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so they land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan worships a pop star who dances with skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of an image or extreme devotion to a person, and an idol is an icon.

clue.text: Smashing park visits with family east of Tring

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a home, so the park word goes inside the others

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a rec is a recreation ground, a public park
kin are relatives

indicators.note: in an across entry east is the right-hand end, so the place name's last letter

parts.note: the final letter of Tring, a town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A family day out to a park just east of the Hertfordshire town of Tring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' sounds like British praise, meaning great, but here it is literal destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecking something means destroying it, breaking it to pieces, which is what smashing it does.

clue.text: Duck, say, knocked over by eccentric cycling

indicators.note: something knocked over ends upside down, so the short word is turned round
cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other, so the word's first letter goes to the back

parts.note: an eccentric person is odd
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A duck, for instance, is bowled over by a weird cyclist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck, say' looks like a bird given as an example, but the comma splits it: Duck is the definition and say gives the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to dodge, lowering or moving to avoid a blow or an awkward question.
